jurisdiction.name: Finland
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Finland implements the EU AI Act through Act 1377/2025, in force since January 2026, which spreads supervision across sector regulators with the Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom) as single point of contact and the Data Protection Ombudsman covering prohibited practices. Strict 2023 amendments to the Administrative Procedure Act limit automated public decisions to rule-based systems. The rest is non-binding: the 2017-2022 national AI programmes, the Ministry of Finance's 2025 generative AI guidelines, defence and education AI documents, the 2026 Digital Compass update, Traficom's sandbox and transparency guidance, and the Financial Supervisory Authority's 2025 review of AI in finance.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Government publications were read through the official publications repository. Not yet verified from the official text: the Data Protection Ombudsman's AI guidance.

instruments.current_status: Informational page; Finnish version last updated 28 September 2026 (English version last updated 13 April 2026). The date recorded is the page's last-updated date; no original publication date is stated. A 2025 draft Government bill would make Traficom responsible for establishing and running the national AI regulatory sandbox (see leads).
instruments.summary: Traficom's guidance page on AI regulatory sandboxes under the EU AI Act. It explains that a sandbox is a supervised, bounded environment where companies can test AI applications under authority guidance before market launch, especially high-risk systems, and that the AI Act requires every member state to establish such sandboxes. It does not itself establish a Finnish sandbox or set admission rules.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Traficom's public information on Finland's AI regulatory sandbox work; the national sandbox legislation is pending (see leads).

instruments.english_title: Act on the Supervision of Certain Artificial Intelligence Systems (1377/2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Finland (Eduskunta); presented by the Government (HE 46/2025), Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment
instruments.current_status: Statute Book of Finland (Suomen säädöskokoelma) 1377/2025, published 29 December 2025; signed 22 December 2025; in force 1 January 2026 (s. 29). Based on Government proposal HE 46/2025 and committee report TaVM 18/2025 (EV 162/2025). Enacted with companion amendments from the same bill (HE 46/2025): Acts 1378/2025 (Market Surveillance Act), 1379/2025 (Enforcement of Fines Act), 1380/2025 (Act on the Financial Supervisory Authority) and 1381/2025 (Act on the Energy Authority). A draft Government bill to amend the act (national AI regulatory sandbox) was consulted on in 2025; see leads.
instruments.summary: Finland's national act supplementing the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It names the market surveillance authorities for high-risk AI systems by sector (including Tukes, Customs, Traficom, the Permit and Supervision Agency, Fimea, the Energy Authority, the Data Protection Ombudsman and the Financial Supervisory Authority), makes the Data Protection Ombudsman the authority for prohibited practices (Art. 5) and Traficom the authority for Art. 50 transparency obligations and the single point of contact. It sets up a sanction-payment board attached to Traficom to impose administrative fines and lays down the fine provisions and appeal routes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national implementing law for the EU AI Act; designates Finland's AI supervisory authorities.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 13-page Statute Book PDF read (pdftotext); title, publication date 29.12.2025, ss. 3-6, 13 and entry into force 1.1.2026 confirmed

instruments.english_title: Act amending the Administrative Procedure Act (487/2023) - automated decision-making
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Finland (Eduskunta); Government proposal HE 145/2022 (Ministry of Justice)
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 May 2023; automated decision-making already in use could continue for 18 months under transitional rules. Paired with Act 488/2023 amending the Information Management Act.
instruments.summary: Adds a new Chapter 8 b (ss. 53 e-53 g) to the Administrative Procedure Act (434/2003) on deciding matters automatically. An authority may issue a final decision by automated data processing without review by a natural person only where no case-by-case discretion is needed (or it has been assessed by an official) and on the basis of pre-set processing rules; requests for rectification may not be decided automatically, the person concerned must be able to request rectification free of charge, and decisions must state that they were made automatically and where the deployment decision is available.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General-law rules on automated (rule-based) decision-making by Finnish public authorities.

instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Finland (Eduskunta); Government proposal HE 145/2022 (Ministry of Finance)
instruments.current_status: Adopted together with Act 487/2023 (HE 145/2022); dates follow the companion Statute Book entries and the Finlex statute page (Statute Book 488/2023).
instruments.summary: Amends the Information Management Act (906/2019) to define the automated decision-making procedure and processing rules (pre-set, human-authored rules) and adds a new Chapter 6 a on deploying and using automated decision-making. It applies to authorities and to private bodies performing public administrative tasks, and requires among other things a documented deployment decision (s. 28 d) to be made publicly available before automated decisions are used.

instruments.english_title: When do you need to disclose the use of AI? (Traficom guidance on AI Act transparency obligations)
instruments.current_status: Guidance page last updated 28 September 2026 (date recorded is the last-updated date; no first-publication date stated). English version available on traficom.fi.
instruments.summary: Traficom guidance, as the authority supervising Art. 50 AI Act transparency obligations, on when providers and deployers must disclose AI use. It explains obligations to tell users they are interacting with AI (chatbots, voice assistants, agents), technically mark AI-generated content, inform people of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation, label deep fakes and disclose AI-generated text on matters of public interest, and how to report suspected breaches. It notes that the obligations apply from 2 August 2026 and are not retroactive.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Supervisory guidance on AI transparency and deepfake labelling from Finland's designated Art. 50 authority.

instruments.english_title: Use of artificial intelligence by financial sector entities (FIN-FSA thematic review)
instruments.current_status: Published 27 June 2025 (public). FIN-FSA's 'Tekoälyn käytön valvonta' (AI use supervision) page links further supervised-entity material, including a March 2026 briefing.
instruments.summary: FIN-FSA thematic review of how banks, insurers, pension institutions, investment firms and consumer lenders use AI, based on a survey of supervised entities. It reports that all large and medium-sized entities use or plan to use AI within two years, mainly generative and general-purpose models in internal processes, identifies data quality, data protection and non-discrimination as key risks, and explains FIN-FSA's role as market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems under the AI Act.

instruments.current_status: Parliamentary document VNS 7/2018 vp; first debated in plenary on 12 December 2018 and further in March 2019 (Parliament open data). The report itself carries no signing date, so only the year is recorded. Historical policy document of the 2015-2019 Government.
instruments.summary: Report of Prime Minister Sipilä's Government to Parliament setting out an ethical information policy for the AI era, decided at the Government's strategy session of 29 January 2018. It describes Finland's national AI programme and information-policy situation, a vision of a 'good life Finland', and lines of action on ethics guiding choices, putting data to use, human-machine interaction, skills, participation and trust, and data-economy competitiveness, intended as the basis for a later prioritised roadmap.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The official statute database, the government publications repository, Parliament's open data, ministries and regulators were searched at national level. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for standards, drafts and consultations, or international agreements. Government publications were checked through the government's publication repository; the Data Protection Ombudsman's AI guidance and the status of the AI sandbox amendment bill remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. valtioneuvosto.fi, vm.fi, tem.fi, okm.fi, stm.fi, lausuntopalvelu.fi and tietosuoja.fi Cloudflare 403 to curl and WebFetch; Government publications read via julkaisut.valtioneuvosto.fi API (API PDF links as source_url). Three domain-named organisations renamed in place (ids kept). Traficom page dates are last-updated dates. Convention 108: SopS 36/1992 with Act 269/1992, recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: Finlex (Statute Book via open-data API and PDFs) searched: Act 1377/2025 on the supervision of certain AI systems (AI Act implementation), Acts 487/2023 and 488/2023 on automated decision-making in public administration recorded; AI sandbox amendment bill and AI advisory-services bill held as leads. No criminal-law deepfake provision or other AI-specific law found.; Government: Government publications repository searched through its own API (tekoäly, artificial intelligence, generatiivinen tekoäly, AuroraAI, tekoälyaika): national AI strategy line recorded (2017 Age of AI, 2019 AI Programme final report, 2022 AI 4.0 final report), 2018 Government report to Parliament on information policy and AI, 2026 Digital Compass update, AuroraAI perspectives, Ministry of Finance generative-AI guidelines and central-government AI guide, DVV Secure AI Development Handbook. Research and study reports (e.g. Government analysis-series studies on algorithmic discrimination) excluded as research rather than governance documents.; Ministries: Parliament open data searched for AI items (VNS 7/2018 recorded; HE 46/2025 enacted; no later AI bill found in plenary agenda titles). Ministry of Finance (GenAI guidance 2025, ethics guidance 2023, AI advisory bill), Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment (AI Act implementation, strategy programmes) and Prime Minister's Office (2026 AI roadmap rapporteur) covered via search and the publications repository API; their own web pages were inaccessible. Defence (2020 AI strategic guidelines) and Education and Culture (2026 citizens' AI competence framework) recorded from the publications repository; Ministry of Justice items found were working-group reports on automated decision-making that led to Acts 487-488/2023 (not recorded separately); health, interior and labour: no AI governance document found beyond research reports.; Regulators: Traficom (AI Act single point of contact; transparency and sandbox guidance pages reviewed), FIN-FSA (2025 AI thematic review reviewed), Data Protection Ombudsman (own site blocked; latest decisions listed on Finlex checked, none AI-specific; lead). National Cyber Security Centre (Traficom): only research reports on AI and cyber security found (2022, 2024), not guidance; competition authority: nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: valtioneuvosto.fi, vm.fi, tem.fi, okm.fi, stm.fi and lausuntopalvelu.fi web pages (403 bot challenge to curl and WebFetch; publications reached via the repository API instead); tietosuoja.fi (403); eduskunta.fi bill tracking for the AI sandbox amendment bill (not reached in time); kkv.fi (only searched indirectly); Finlex Data Protection Ombudsman year listings (rendered by script; only the latest-decisions list was checked). Could not verify: Data Protection Ombudsman AI guidance (tietosuoja.fi blocked); Status and text of the 2025 AI sandbox amendment draft (VN/31658/2024; consulted April-June 2025). standards, drafts, international: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): Several ministry websites blocked access, so government publications were read through the official publications repository, and the Data Protection Ombudsman's AI guidance could not be checked.
